A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same OServe system. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables, and appendices support comparison, including matching material relocated between versions.

before.justification: v1 reports original serving experiments, latency and throughput measurements, workload-prediction results, ablations, and appendix evaluations.

after.justification: v2 retains those original empirical results and adds spatial and temporal heterogeneity sensitivity experiments in Section 6.3.

M1.justification: The two-level scheduler, k-means/LSTM workload predictor, greedy switching procedure, KV-cache handling, and appendix Algorithms 1–2 are unchanged. Moving the system overview into Section 3 does not introduce a method component.

E1.justification: v2 adds controlled Azure-derived test scenarios: five workload mixtures with different spatial skew and four temporal sequences of those mixtures. These extend input-condition coverage while retaining the existing datasets and workload types.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain vLLM (static), vLLM (reload), Llumnix, Dynamo+vLLM, and the existing predictor and exhaustive-search comparators. The added sensitivity study reuses vLLM (static).

E3.justification: The added sensitivity protocol evaluates Llama2-70B on 16 GPUs using controlled workload proportions and temporal transitions, characterized by spatial and temporal coefficients of variation. Previously reported experimental settings are retained.

E4.justification: Section 6.3 and Tables 1–2 add targeted analyses of how performance benefits vary with spatial skew and temporal workload changes. Existing component ablations, prediction comparisons, optimality checks, and homogeneous-workload analysis remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Existing statistical reporting is retained. The new tables add point speedups without repeated-run counts or uncertainty estimates; their CV values describe workload variability, not uncertainty in measured performance.

E6.justification: Tables 1–2 add five spatial speedups ranging from 1.14× to 2.66× and four temporal speedups ranging from 1.23× to 1.98× over vLLM (static). Existing main-text and appendix results are unchanged; these are additional settings, not same-setting performance improvements.

T1.justification: The flow-network constraints, capacity normalization, optimization objective, and appendix mathematical examples are unchanged. The added empirical CV descriptors introduce no formal theoretical development or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the scheduling and switching contributions and the headline improvement of up to 2×, averaging 1.5×. The sensitivity study supplies additional support without redefining those core claims.

C2.justification: v2 interprets the new sensitivity results as showing increasingly effective workload-aware deployment and assignment as heterogeneity grows, attributing the widening advantage to static deployments' increasing mismatch. Existing limitations and extensibility discussions are retained.

D1.justification: For the added sensitivity experiments, Tables 1–2 document exact SILO/LILO/SISO/LISO percentages and the ordering of workload mixtures used to construct temporal traces. Existing implementation, profiling, hardware, and code-link information is unchanged.

R1.justification: The reference list and substantive research positioning are unchanged. Extended related work moves from Appendix B to Appendix A without adding or removing cited works.

P1.justification: The overview moves from v1 Appendix A into v2 Section 3 with light prose editing. Section and appendix references are updated, the publication notice changes, and a sensitivity-analysis paragraph is added; the remaining narrative is largely retained.

P2.justification: v2 adds two sensitivity tables and moves the overview diagram from Figure 16 to Figure 3, resizing it and correcting LiveServe labels and section references. Existing result plots retain their content, while figures, the case-study table, and surrounding text undergo relocation and reflow.

improvement.justification: The sensitivity study supplements v1's trace experiments and ablations with targeted evidence about when OServe benefits most. Bringing the corrected overview into the main text also improves accessibility. The gain is limited: the new study covers one model/cluster configuration, and its tables do not clearly identify the performance metric underlying speedup or report uncertainty.
